headline: Highest risk is medium: Airflow can feed untrusted outputs into Rasa, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways; no direct evidence of shared storage or compliance mismatch.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can orchestrate external data flows and has broad network egress, while Rasa ingests conversational text/voice via messaging channels. A direct shared channel is not documented, but if Airflow outputs are routed into Rasa without sanitization, attacker-controlled content could steer downstream behavior. Uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF Airflow task output is forwarded into a Rasa channel or webhook
IF Rasa treats that forwarded content as conversational input without sanitization
mitigations: Add an allowlist filter on Airflow-to-Rasa payload fields
Strip instructions and markup from any Airflow-generated text
Route only structured JSON, not free text
Review one sample end-to-end message path
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to forwarded messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow touches no declared sensitive data classes, and Rasa touches text/voice only. There is no documented shared workspace or authenticated principal, so a leakage path is not established. The main concern is accidental forwarding of pipeline text into chat channels, which is limited without evidence of sensitive data.
conditions: IF Airflow tasks contain secrets or regulated data in logs or outputs
IF those outputs are copied into Rasa-connected channels
mitigations: Redact secrets from Airflow logs
Disable verbose task output in chat channels
Check one sample message for sensitive fields
Limit Rasa channel payloads to non-sensitive summaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, while Rasa has allowlisted egress and no multiple-instance support. The profiles do not show overlapping filesystem or git writes, so direct write conflict is not evidenced. A coordination issue is still possible if both are pointed at the same mutable external API, but that is not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API or queue
IF no external locking or idempotency key is used
mitigations: Assign separate output destinations
Add idempotency keys to shared writes
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Check for duplicate side effects in a test run

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate pipeline facts or status text, and Rasa can consume text as dialogue input. If Rasa treats Airflow output as authoritative, a bad upstream task can cascade into incorrect responses or actions. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default integrations and merits medium severity.
conditions: IF Airflow-generated text is injected into Rasa training, rules, or live dialogue context
IF Rasa does not verify the upstream content before responding
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Rasa ingestion
Mark Airflow outputs as untrusted metadata
Compare outputs against a schema
Sample-check one downstream response path
requires-engineering: add automated provenance verification

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is documented for either agent. Airflow lists no touched data classes, and Rasa lists text/voice only, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway in this pair. The other agent is not separately cited because no cross-border or regulated-data flow is shown.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through either agent
IF a separate policy or residency constraint is introduced
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Review retention settings before deployment
Confirm regional hosting for any regulated data
